title: Dazor — watched chats
goal: See which Teams chats have said something since I last summarised them, and open one.

zones.name: header
zones.purpose: The product's own hero: the ecosystem mark, "Welcome to Dazor" with the name in the brand gradient, and one capped line saying what it does. Plus the single creating action: watch another chat, pasted as a Teams link.

zones.name: content
zones.purpose: One tile per watched chat, following the card anatomy and stopping at the levels it has: the chat's Teams topic as the name, then a footer line saying what is waiting and when it arrived. No badge and no second line for the date: a count in a solid chip was the loudest thing on a page whose only real action is elsewhere, and a date on its own row had the rank of a fact. <LinkTile> rather than a hand-built card, because the tile has to be openable by keyboard and carry an overflow menu, and that composition already exists.

zones.name: notice
zones.purpose: Sign-in state, because every count on this screen depends on it. Rendered only when the Microsoft sign-in has expired: a signed-in person should never see a banner about signing in.

zones.name: dialogs
zones.purpose: Adding a chat is a form (the pasted link, with the server's parse error shown on the field). Stopping watching is destructive in the one way that matters and says so: the summaries stay, the record of how far you had read does not.

states.loading: Skeleton tiles in the grid, and the template's count=null so it does not flash the empty state at every visit
states.empty: EmptyState via the template's empty prop, icon=message, inviting the first chat to be added
states.error: Alert tone=danger through the template's error prop, naming what Graph refused and offering a retry

data: chats: id (19:...@thread.v2), label, unreadCount, newestUnreadAt, lastSummarizedAt — from the digest server, which reads Microsoft Graph
auth: signedIn, needLogin, username — from the shared Graph token cache via the server
openQuestions: A chat nobody has posted in for months still costs one Graph page per refresh. If the list grows past a handful, the counts need to be fetched on demand rather than for the whole list.
Nothing polls: the counts are as fresh as the last time the screen was opened. Whether that is enough depends on how the tool ends up being used.

behaviours.given: a watched chat with messages arrived since its last summary
behaviours.then: its card says how many are new and when the newest arrived
behaviours.why: The list exists to answer 'is there anything to do' without opening anything.
behaviours.pendingReason: No screen test yet. The page renders from the API and the count comes straight from the same watermark the detail screen is tested against; a test here needs the fixture server the page audit uses. Closes when apps/teams-digest/src/layouts/ChatsPage.test.tsx exists.

behaviours.given: a chat the signed-in person is no longer a participant of
behaviours.then: the card says that plainly instead of showing an empty or stale summary
behaviours.why: Delegated Chat.Read only reaches chats you are in. That refusal is a fact about the world, not a bug to paper over.
behaviours.pendingReason: Same as above: needs the fixture-backed screen test. The refusal path is already exercised by the visual baseline chats.phone, which is a picture and not an assertion.
